objective.statement: Diagnose and fix the flaky login test so that it passes consistently.
objective.success_definition: The login test no longer exhibits flaky behavior; it passes (or fails) deterministically and consistently across runs.

goals.statement: Identify the root cause of the flaky behavior in the login test.
acceptance: The root cause of the intermittent test behavior has been identified.

goals.statement: Modify the login test (or the code it exercises) so the flakiness is resolved.
acceptance: The login test runs deterministically with consistent results across runs.

assumptions.statement: There exists a specific, identifiable test for the login flow referred to as 'the login test'.
'Flaky' means the test intermittently passes or fails without changes to the code under test.
The source of the flakiness (test code vs. production login code) is unspecified, so the fix may need to touch either.

open_questions.question: How many consistent runs (locally or in CI) are required for the test to be considered 'fixed'?
options: a defined CI stability criterion set by the team

open_questions.question: Is the fix expected to be confined to the test, or may it also change the production login code if the flakiness originates there?
options: test and/or production code as needed

verification.spec: Review the diagnosis to confirm the root cause of the flaky behavior has been identified.
verification.expected: Root cause of the flakiness is identified and documented.

verification.spec: Run the login test repeatedly (multiple iterations) and observe the results.
verification.expected: The login test produces consistent, deterministic results across runs; no intermittent failures.

deliverables.description: A fix that resolves the flakiness of the login test.

factors: Flaky-test root causes are often nondeterministic and hard to reproduce.
A fix may mask the symptom (e.g., added retries/sleeps) rather than resolve the underlying timing, environment, or dependency issue.
